title: Lesson 3 · The Verb
blurb: Finding verbs; action/being/state; transitive, intransitive & copulative; verb mistakes.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“Birds fly south.”
items.explain: “fly” tells what the birds do — it is the verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“The baby sleeps.”
items.explain: “sleeps” is the verb — it tells what the baby does.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“Farmers grow wheat.”
items.explain: “grow” tells what the farmers do.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“She sings sweetly.”
items.explain: “sings” is the action word — the verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“We are happy.”
items.explain: “are” is the verb (a being verb).

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“The dog chased the cat.”
items.explain: “chased” tells the action — the verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“Snow melts in spring.”
items.explain: “melts” is the verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“They built a treehouse.”
items.explain: “built” tells what they did — the verb.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“George runs.”
items.explain: “runs” is something done — action.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“I am.”
items.explain: “am” expresses being.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“The rocket launched.”
items.explain: “launched” is an action.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“They are students.”
items.explain: “are” expresses being.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“The house belongs to us.”
items.explain: “belongs” names a condition, not a deed — state.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“Water freezes.”
items.explain: “freezes” is a change that happens — action.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“Columbus discovered America.”
items.explain: “discovered” takes an object (America), so it is transitive.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“Horses run.”
items.explain: “run” needs no object, so it is intransitive.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“The soup tastes good.”
items.explain: “tastes” links “soup” to “good” — copulative.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“She wrote a letter.”
items.explain: “wrote” takes an object (a letter) — transitive.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“The baby smiled.”
items.explain: “smiled” needs no object — intransitive.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“He is a doctor.”
items.explain: “is” links “He” to “doctor” — copulative.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“Farmers plant corn.”
items.explain: “plant” takes an object (corn) — transitive.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“The sun shines.”
items.explain: “shines” needs no object — intransitive.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“The weather grew cold.”
items.explain: “grew” links “weather” to “cold” — copulative.

items.prompt:
Is the verb transitive, intransitive, or copulative?

“Dogs chase cars.”
items.explain: “chase” takes an object (cars) — transitive.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“I have ___ that movie.”
items.explain: With the helper “have,” use the participle: have seen.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“She ___ to the store yesterday.”
items.explain: Past time, no helper: went.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“He has ___ home.”
items.explain: With the helper “has,” use the participle: has gone.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“They ___ the ball over the fence.”
items.explain: The past of throw is threw (never “throwed”).

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“We have ___ dinner already.”
items.explain: With the helper “have,” use the participle: have eaten.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“The bell has ___.”
items.explain: With the helper “has,” use the participle: has rung.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“He ___ his work well yesterday.”
items.explain: Past time, no helper: did (never “done” alone).

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“You ___ there when it happened.”
items.explain: With “you,” always use were.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“Rivers flow to the sea.”
items.explain: “flow” tells what the rivers do — the verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“The clock ticks.”
items.explain: “ticks” tells what the clock does — the verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“Lightning flashed brightly.”
items.explain: “flashed” tells the action — the verb.

items.prompt:
Which word is the verb?

“Bees buzz softly.”
items.explain: “buzz” tells what the bees do — the verb.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“Snow falls.”
items.explain: “falls” is something done — action.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“They are ready.”
items.explain: “are” expresses being.

items.prompt:
Does this verb express action, being, or state?

“The gate remains open.”
items.explain: “remains” names a condition, not a deed — state.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“The sun has ___.”
items.explain: With the helper “has,” use the participle: has risen.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“They have ___ the song.”
items.explain: With the helper “have,” use the participle: have sung.

items.prompt:
Choose the correct verb:

“I have ___ a letter.”
items.explain: With the helper “have,” use the participle: have written.
